'''Diana Marcela Bolaños Rodríguez''' is a Colombian [[marine biologist]] who has studied and classified various types of [[platyhelminths]]. She was a recipient of the [[L'Oréal-UNESCO Awards for Women in Science|L'Oréal-UNESCO Fellowship for Women in Science]] in 2010, was selected as Colombian biologist of the year in 2012, and in 2013 was named by the [[BBC]] as one of the top ten women in science in Latin America.

==Biography==
Bolaños Rodríguez was born in 1980 in [[Bogotá]], [[Colombia]], and grew up there.<ref name="L´Oréal Prize">{{cite news| title=La investigadora colombiana Marcela Bolaños, premio Unesco – L´Oréal for Women in Science| url=http://www.dicyt.com/noticias/la-investigadora-colombiana-marcela-bolanos-premio-unesco-l-oreal-for-women-in-science| access-date=15 November 2015| publisher=Agencia de Noticias para la Difusión de la Ciencia y la Tecnología| date=5 March 2010| location=Salamanca, Spain| language=es}}</ref> At age 19, she enrolled in the [[Universidad Jorge Tadeo Lozano]] at the campus in [[Santa Marta]] on the [[Caribbean]] side of Colombia. After completing her undergraduate work with a thesis on [[flatworm]]s,<ref name="Plaza Capital">{{cite journal| last1=Toro Vesga| first1=María Alejandra| title=Una colombiana con mucha ciencia| url=http://portal.urosario.edu.co/pla_2004_2008/articulo.php?articulo=1630| access-date=15 November 2015| issue=32| journal=Plaza Capital| publisher=Universidad Del Rosario| location=Bogotá, Colombia| issn=1900-5113| language=es| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151115171547/http://portal.urosario.edu.co/pla_2004_2008/articulo.php?articulo=1630| archive-date=15 November 2015| url-status=dead}}</ref> in 2003, Bolaños continued her education at the [[University of New Hampshire]] (UNH) in the United States.<ref name="biologist of the year">{{cite news| title=Diana Marcela Bolaños, profesora del Programa de Biología escogida como Bióloga del Año en Colombia| url=http://www.mineducacion.gov.co/cvn/1665/w3-article-312450.html| access-date=15 November 2015| publisher=Min Educacion| date=27 September 2012| location=Cartagena, Colombia| language=es| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140910130301/http://www.mineducacion.gov.co/cvn/1665/w3-article-312450.html| archive-date=10 September 2014| url-status=dead}}</ref> She received her PhD in [[zoology]] from UNH in [[Durham, New Hampshire]], in 2008 with an Award for Excellence in Research from the Department of Zoology.<ref name="L´Oréal Prize" /> Her research focused on polyclad flatworms,<ref name="current position-English source">{{cite news| title=Interview with Colombian scientist Diana Marcela Bolaños| url=https://www.sdbonline.org/sites/SDBe-news/Spring2012/bolanos.html| access-date=15 November 2015| publisher=Society for Developmental Biology| date=Spring 2012| location=Bethesda, Maryland}}</ref> a marine worm which is unique in its ability to generate tissue through [[stem cell]]s.<ref name="L´Oréal Prize" />

She married an American, Joseph Dunn,<ref name="husband's name">{{cite news| title=Las 100 colombianas con más 'batallas ganadas'| url=https://www.eltiempo.com/archivo/documento/CMS-8021977| access-date=16 November 2015| publisher=El Tiempo| date=29 September 2010| location=Bogotá, Colombia| language=es}}</ref> whom she had met while in New Hampshire, and in 2008 returned to Colombia to continue her research, completing a database of flatworm species and their [[taxonomic groups]]. Bolaños also took a teaching post as a visiting professor for the [[University of Los Andes (Colombia)|University of the Andes]] (Uniandes).<ref name="Plaza Capital" />

In 2010, she was awarded a [[L'Oréal-UNESCO Awards for Women in Science|L'Oréal-UNESCO Fellowship for Women in Science]]<ref name="L´Oréal Prize" /><ref name=UNESCO>{{cite web| title=L'OREAL-UNESCO Awards and Fellowships for Women in Science 2010 to be presented at UNESCO| url=http://www.unesco.org/new/en/media-services/single-view/news/loreal_unesco_awards_and_fellowships_for_women_in_science_2010_to_be_presented_at_unesco/#.Vkn8u-K2oVI| publisher=UNESCO| access-date=16 November 2015| location=Geneva, Switzerland| date=25 February 2010}}</ref> and she used the award to complete her postdoctoral research at Uniandes. Bolaños then took a post as an assistant professor in the Biology Program at the [[Universidad de Cartagena]].<ref name="current position-English source" /> In 2012, she was named Colombian biologist of the year<ref name="biologist of the year" /> and in 2013 was named one of the top ten women scientists in [[Latin America]] by the BBC.<ref name=BBC>{{cite news| title=Ecuatoriana entre las 10 científicas más destacadas de Latinoamérica| url=https://www.eluniverso.com/vida-estilo/2013/10/18/nota/1598816/ecuatoriana-10-cientificas-mas-destacadas-latinoamerica| access-date=15 November 2015| publisher=El Universo| date=18 October 2013| location=Quito, Ecuador| language=es}}</ref>

Bolaños has continued her research and is working on comparisons between polyclads, [[planarian]]s and other types of [[platyhelminths]] and their abilities to regenerate.<ref name="current position-English source" /> In addition, she has published numerous articles in international, peer-reviewed journals such as ''[[Evolution & Development]]'', the ''[[Journal of Natural History]]'' and ''[[Zootaxa]]'' in the areas of [[evolution]] and [[systematics|biological systematics]],<ref name="biologist of the year" /> as well as continuing her education at courses such as the [[Society for Developmental Biology]] short course held in [[Montevideo]], [[Uruguay]].<ref name="current position-English source" /> The flatworm Bisacculosuteri marcelae was named in her honor in 2019.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ramos-Sánchez|first1=Mariela|last2=Bahia|first2=Juliana|last3=Bastida-Zavala|first3=J. Rolando|date=2019-11-18|title=New genus, new species and new records of marine acotylean flatworms (Platyhelminthes: Polycladida: Acotylea) from Oaxaca, southern Mexican Pacific|url=https://doi.org/10.11646/zootaxa.4700.1.2|journal=[[Zootaxa]]|volume=4700|issue=1|pages=30–58|doi=10.11646/zootaxa.4700.1.2|pmid=32229990 |issn=1175-5334|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
